summary: Backend-only testing of Lex Stage 2 (preview). I ran the unit tests (44/44 pass), the Stage 1 smoke tests (9/9 pass) and 10 new live pytest checks in two files. Those checks used 8 Lex chat calls in total, within the 10-call limit, all from fictional users that were cloned and then deleted. 9 of 10 live checks pass. The one failure: the risk classifier treats an illegal lock-out by a landlord (category 'property', no keyword match) as LOW risk. So when research fails, the deterministic 'couldn't check' note is not added and [CONFIDENCE: HIGH] is kept. The same quota-exhaustion path with a clear high-risk keyword (section 21 / evict, streaming) works: research_status quota_exhausted, deterministic note added, no [n] markers, confidence downgraded to MEDIUM, no Tavily calls made.

critical.issue: Urgent housing scenarios are classified LOW risk. Examples: 'landlord changed the locks and put my belongings on the street' (category=property), 'landlord kicked me out', 'threw me out'. HIGH_RISK_RE has no lock-out wording and 'property' is not in HIGH_RISK_CATEGORIES. Live result with quota_exhausted: no deterministic research note and the answer ended with [CONFIDENCE: HIGH]. That breaks requirement (c): high-risk => confidence not HIGH plus a clear warning. The LLM did write its own 'I can't check live official sources right now' sentence, so the customer saw some limitation text, but it is not guaranteed.

minor.issue: Answers still give definitive conclusions (e.g. 'a landlord cannot validly use a section 21 notice from 1 May 2026'), even though research_block tells the model not to. The [SOURCES: ...] tail still lists Acts that were never retrieved. This is prompt-only enforcement, with no server-side check.
This message counts as high risk only because 'refusing' matches refus\w*. Classifying by incidental words like this is fragile.

The deterministic note and the confidence downgrade appear only in done.full_text, not in the streamed tokens. The frontend must replace the streamed text with full_text, otherwise the user never sees the note. Frontend was not tested in this round.

CORS returns access-control-allow-origin '*' together with allow-credentials true. Auth uses a Bearer token, not httpOnly cookies. Passwords are bcrypt $2b$ (OK). I did not run the brute-force lockout test, to avoid locking the shared test account.

verified_passing: POST /api/lex/chat returns session_id, response, citations, saved_reminders, model, connected_session_id, research_status ('ok') and jurisdiction_check (False for an England ACAS question)
ACAS regression: 'dismissed on 2 November 2026 in England' => reminder 'Contact ACAS (tribunal time limit)', due 2027-05-01T09:00+01:00; the answer contains '1 May 2027'
Streaming: meta event has research_status 'ok'; done.full_text present; markers {1,2} are a subset of citations {1..5}

Quota exhausted (regular and streaming): research_status quota_exhausted, citations [], no Tavily rows written. The Tavily count was recorded and restored both times (now 118 = original 106 + 12 real calls from this run)

Jurisdiction conflict: Scotland profile + Cardiff deposit => jurisdiction_check true; the answer opens with 'Which UK nation is the rented property in — Wales (Cardiff) or somewhere else?'; the profile jurisdiction stays 'scotland'

Cross-conversation: a fictional agent name from session A is not used in a new session B; another user's GET /api/lex/sessions/{A} does not expose it; the owner can read it; a follow-up inside session A does recall it
GET /api/admin/llm-spend returns total_gbp, calls, by_model, top_users, cost_basis {measured, estimated, flat_rate} and cost_basis_note; non-admin gets 401/403
llm_usage: every LLM row from this run has measured:true and tokens_source 'provider'; Tavily rows are not_applicable/measured:false; tokens_source always matches the measured flag
GET /api/admin/lex-lessons: 46 lessons, 25 with needs_review and a review_reason
action_items: Widen lex_safety.HIGH_RISK_RE to cover lock-out / illegal eviction wording, e.g. 'changed the locks', 'locked (me )?out', 'kicked (me )?out', 'threw me out', 'thrown out', 'belongings (out|on the street)', 'unlawful eviction', 'disrepair', 'mould', 'gas leak'. Consider adding 'property' (or housing topics) to HIGH_RISK_CATEGORIES. Add a unit test for this.
Optional: when research has failed, strip or annotate the [SOURCES: ...] tail so it does not look like verified sources
Make sure the frontend stream handler replaces the streamed text with done.full_text so the deterministic note and confidence downgrade are visible
critical_code_review_comments: risk_level depends on keywords only; the most urgent housing scenario (lock-out) falls through to low
In /lex/chat, if rag_research raises, research keeps the default {'status':'unavailable'}, so citations stay [] and the research block is applied. Correct.
server.py is over 17k lines (pre-existing); the new Stage 2 logic is kept in lex_safety.py, which is good
seed_data_creation: Created and then deleted 3 fictional users (iter45.a/b/scot@stage2-fictional-test.co.uk) and their conversations and reminders. tavily_usage for 2026-11 was restored after both exhaustion simulations. No seed or production data was modified.
context_for_next_testing_agent: 8 Lex calls used (budget 10). To re-check the fix offline at no cost: python -c "import lex_safety as s; print(s.risk_level('my landlord changed the locks', 'property'))" should print 'high'. The live tests clone test@advocate.app with tier plus; the module fixture cleans up. Known pre-existing failures (test_lex_routing, test_iter41 acas dup) were not run or counted.
rca of the issue: Repro: set db.tavily_usage{month:2026-11}.count=100000, then POST /api/lex/chat with category=property and the message 'my landlord in Bristol changed the locks while I was out and put my belongings on the street. What are my rights right now?'. risk_level returns 'low' (no regex match, and property is not a high-risk category). finalize_answer only adds the note and downgrades [CONFIDENCE: HIGH] when risk=='high' or the answer claims verification, so neither happens. Fix: extend HIGH_RISK_RE / HIGH_RISK_CATEGORIES.
